---
title: "Pull-Request Workflow"
---

7 requirement(s) in this category.

### PR-001 — Target master with small, self-contained PRs {#sec-pr-001}

**Mathlib + PhysLean** · Level **SHALL**

A PR SHALL target the `master` branch of the upstream repository and SHALL be kept small and self-contained; the smaller the better.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The PR base branch is `master`.
- The PR is one coherent, self-contained change.

**Rationale.** Small PRs against master are reviewable and keep the mainline releasable.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/how-to-contribute.html>

---

### PR-002 — master always compiles {#sec-pr-002}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

It is essential that everything in `master` compiles without errors; a PR SHALL NOT be merged in a state that breaks the build.

**Acceptance criteria**

- CI is green on the PR before merge.
- The change builds locally with `lake build`.

**Rationale.** `master` is the production version depended on by the whole ecosystem.

**Verify.** lake build

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/how-to-contribute.html>

---

### PR-003 — Build and cache locally before pushing {#sec-pr-003}

**Mathlib + PhysLean** · Level **SHALL**

Before pushing, the contributor SHALL build locally and use the compilation cache: run `lake exe cache get` to download built dependencies and `lake build` to build; after adding new files run `lake exe mk_all`. PhysLean setup uses `lake update; lake exe cache get; lake build`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- `lake exe cache get` and `lake build` were run locally and pass.
- New files were registered with `lake exe mk_all`.

**Rationale.** Local builds catch errors before they reach CI and reviewers.

**Verify.** lake exe cache get && lake build

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/how-to-contribute.html>

---

### PR-004 — Run the linters locally {#sec-pr-004}

**Mathlib + PhysLean** · Level **SHALL**

Before submitting, the contributor SHALL run the project's linters locally and fix all reported issues. Mathlib: the style linter and `shake`; PhysLean: `lake exe lint_all` and `./scripts/lint-style.sh`. CI runs the linters on every PR.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The style linter passes locally.
- PhysLean: `lake exe lint_all` and `./scripts/lint-style.sh` pass.

**Rationale.** Linters enforce the style and structural rules automatically; running them locally avoids review round-trips.

**Verify.** lake exe lint_all && ./scripts/lint-style.sh

**Source.** <http://physlib.io/getting-started>

---

### PR-005 — "easy" PR criteria {#sec-pr-005}

**Mathlib** · Level **INFO**

A PR MAY be labelled `easy` when it adds a single lemma or fixes typos, with a diff generally under 25 lines, changing no existing definitions or theorem statements and adding no new definitions, files, `simp` lemmas, or instances.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The diff is small (~25 lines) and adds no new defs/files/simp/instances.
- No existing statement is changed.

**Rationale.** The `easy` label routes trivial PRs to a fast lane and sets reviewer expectations.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/how-to-contribute.html>

---

### PR-006 — Fork or branch workflow {#sec-pr-006}

**Mathlib + PhysLean** · Level **MAY**

A contributor MAY contribute either by (a) forking the repository, pushing to the fork, and opening a PR upstream, or (b) requesting collaborator access and pushing a feature branch (e.g. `feat(your-name): updating spacetime`) on the main repository, then opening a PR.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Changes arrive as a PR from either a fork or an upstream feature branch.

**Rationale.** Both routes are supported; collaborator access streamlines repeat contributors.

**Source.** <http://physlib.io/getting-started>

---

### PR-007 — Squash-merge; do not rebase after review starts {#sec-pr-007}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHOULD**

Mathlib PRs are squashed on merge, so intermediate commit history is not retained. Once a PR has seen review activity, the author SHOULD NOT rebase or squash, as that obfuscates the review history.

**Acceptance criteria**

- No rebase/squash is performed after review begins.
- The author relies on squash-on-merge for a clean final history.

**Rationale.** Preserving the post-review commit graph keeps the review auditable.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/how-to-contribute.html>
